    if device.type == "cuda":
        logging.info("GPU: %s", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))

    train_frame = load_lob_frame(Path(cfg.train_path))
    valid_frame = load_lob_frame(Path(cfg.valid_path))

    train_frame, train_seq_ids = _maybe_limit_sequences(train_frame, cfg.train_sequences_limit, cfg.seed)
    valid_frame, valid_seq_ids = _maybe_limit_sequences(valid_frame, cfg.valid_sequences_limit, cfg.seed)

    logging.info(
        "Loaded frames: train_rows=%d valid_rows=%d train_seq=%d valid_seq=%d",
        train_frame.height,
        valid_frame.height,
        train_seq_ids.size,
        valid_seq_ids.size,
    )

    pipeline = GRUFeaturePipeline(
        GRUFeatureConfig(
            warmup_steps=cfg.warmup_steps,
            rolling_window=cfg.rolling_window,
            n_instrument_bins=cfg.instrument_bins,
            eps=cfg.eps,
            drop_p0_p6=cfg.drop_p0_p6,
        )
    )
    train_batch = pipeline.fit_transform(train_frame)
    valid_batch = pipeline.transform(valid_frame)

    loss_cfg = LossConfig(
        beta_t1=cfg.beta_t1_mse,
        eps_weights=cfg.eps,
        eps_std=1e-5,
        sequence_reweighting=cfg.sequence_reweighting,
    )

    train_dataset = SequenceTensorDataset(train_batch)
    train_loader = _build_loader(
        train_dataset,
        batch_size=cfg.batch_size,
        shuffle=True,
        num_workers=cfg.num_workers,
        pin_memory=cfg.pin_memory,
    )

    model = AutoRegDualHeadGRU(
        input_dim=train_batch.features.shape[2],
        n_instrument_bins=pipeline.instrument_bins,
        instrument_embedding_dim=cfg.instrument_embedding_dim,
        hidden_size=cfg.hidden_size,
        num_layers=cfg.num_layers,
        variational_dropout=cfg.variational_dropout,
        recurrent_dropout=cfg.recurrent_dropout,
        head_hidden_size=cfg.head_hidden_size,
    )
    model = model.to(device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
    model = maybe_compile_model(model, enabled=cfg.torch_compile)

    history: list[dict[str, float | str]] = []
    best_state: dict[str, torch.Tensor] | None = None
    best_score = -float("inf")
    best_epoch = 0
    best_stage = ""
    epochs_no_improve = 0
    best_score_for_patience = -float("inf")

    # Teacher stage (weighted MSE).
    optimizer = AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=cfg.lr_teacher, weight_decay=cfg.weight_decay)
    train_start = time.perf_counter()
    total_free_epochs = cfg.epochs_free_mse + cfg.epochs_free_pearson
    total_epochs = cfg.epochs_teacher + total_free_epochs

    for epoch in range(1, total_epochs + 1):
        if epoch <= cfg.epochs_teacher:
            train_row = train_epoch_teacher(
                model=model,
                loader=train_loader,
                optimizer=optimizer,
                device=device,
                cfg=cfg,
                loss_cfg=loss_cfg,
            )
        else:
            if epoch == cfg.epochs_teacher + 1:
                optimizer = AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=cfg.lr_free_mse, weight_decay=cfg.weight_decay)
                logging.info("Switching to free-run MSE stage.")
            if epoch == cfg.epochs_teacher + cfg.epochs_free_mse + 1 and cfg.epochs_free_pearson > 0:
                optimizer = AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=cfg.lr_free_pearson, weight_decay=cfg.weight_decay)
                logging.info("Switching to free-run Pearson stage.")

            free_epoch_ix = epoch - (cfg.epochs_teacher + 1)
            tf_prob = _tf_prob_for_epoch(
                epoch_ix=free_epoch_ix,
                total_epochs=max(total_free_epochs, 1),
                tf_start=cfg.teacher_forcing_start,
                tf_end=cfg.teacher_forcing_end,
            )
            use_pearson_loss = free_epoch_ix >= cfg.epochs_free_mse
            train_row = train_epoch_free(
                model=model,
                loader=train_loader,
                optimizer=optimizer,
                device=device,
                cfg=cfg,
                loss_cfg=loss_cfg,
                teacher_forcing_prob=tf_prob,
                use_pearson_loss=use_pearson_loss,
            )

        preds_valid = predict_free_run_seq_major(
            model=model,
            features=valid_batch.features,
            instrument_ids=valid_batch.instrument_ids,
            batch_size=max(32, min(cfg.batch_size, 512)),
            device=device,
        )
        valid_scores = evaluate_on_batch(preds_valid, valid_batch)

        row: dict[str, float | str] = {
            "epoch": float(epoch),
            "stage": str(train_row["stage"]),
            "train_loss": float(train_row["train_loss"]),
            "grad_norm": float(train_row["grad_norm"]),
            "lr": float(train_row["lr"]),
            "valid_t0": float(valid_scores["t0"]),
            "valid_t1": float(valid_scores["t1"]),
            "valid_weighted_pearson": float(valid_scores["weighted_pearson"]),
        }
        if "teacher_forcing_prob" in train_row:
            row["teacher_forcing_prob"] = float(train_row["teacher_forcing_prob"])
        history.append(row)

        current = float(valid_scores["weighted_pearson"])
        if current > best_score:
            best_score = current
            best_epoch = epoch
            best_stage = str(train_row["stage"])
            best_state = _clone_state(model)
            torch.save(best_state, run_dir / "best_model.pt")

        if epoch > cfg.epochs_teacher:
            if current > (best_score_for_patience + cfg.early_stopping_min_delta):
                best_score_for_patience = current
                epochs_no_improve = 0
            else:
                epochs_no_improve += 1

        logging.info(
            "Epoch %d/%d | stage=%s | loss=%.6f | t0=%.6f | t1=%.6f | rho=%.6f | best=%.6f | patience=%d/%d",
            epoch,
            total_epochs,
            row["stage"],
            row["train_loss"],
            row["valid_t0"],
            row["valid_t1"],
            row["valid_weighted_pearson"],
            best_score,
            epochs_no_improve,
            cfg.early_stopping_patience,
        )

        if (
            epoch > cfg.epochs_teacher
            and cfg.early_stopping_patience > 0
            and epochs_no_improve >= cfg.early_stopping_patience
        ):
            logging.info("Early stopping triggered at epoch=%d", epoch)
            break

    train_runtime_sec = float(time.perf_counter() - train_start)
    if best_state is None:
        raise RuntimeError("No checkpoint captured.")

    _load_state(model, best_state)
    preds_valid_best = predict_free_run_seq_major(
        model=model,
        features=valid_batch.features,
        instrument_ids=valid_batch.instrument_ids,
        batch_size=max(32, min(cfg.batch_size, 512)),
        device=device,
    )
    best_scores = evaluate_on_batch(preds_valid_best, valid_batch)

    save_predictions(run_dir / "valid_predictions.parquet", preds_valid_best, valid_batch)

    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
        "run_dir": str(run_dir.relative_to(PROJECT_ROOT)),
        "config": asdict(cfg),
        "train_runtime_seconds": train_runtime_sec,
        "epochs_ran": len(history),
        "best_epoch": best_epoch,
        "best_stage": best_stage,
        "best_valid_scores": best_scores,
        "history": history,
    }

    (run_dir / "metrics.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sort_keys=True),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    logging.info("Finished run: %s", json.dumps(payload["best_valid_scores"], ensure_ascii=False))
    return payload

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate full train/valid predictions from saved ML baseline models."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import joblib
import numpy as np
import polars as pl

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
if str(PROJECT_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_ROOT))

ML_MODEL_ROOT = Path(
    "/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-Predictorium/models/ML_baseline/model_rho_w_0_214271_2026-02-22_22-10-07"
)
ML_SRC_ROOT = ML_MODEL_ROOT / "src"
if str(ML_SRC_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ML_SRC_ROOT))

from src.data import load_lob_frame  # type: ignore
from src.evaluation import score_two_targets  # type: ignore
from src.features import FeatureConfig, engineer_lob_features  # type: ignore


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--train-path", default="/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-Predictorium/data/train.parquet")
    parser.add_argument("--valid-path", default="/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-Predictorium/data/valid.parquet")
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", default="experiments/vendor_features")
    return parser.parse_args()


def target_lag1_by_sequence(target: np.ndarray, seq_ids: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    lag = np.zeros_like(target, dtype=np.float32)
    if target.size <= 1:
        return lag
    same = seq_ids[1:] == seq_ids[:-1]
    lag[1:] = np.where(same, target[:-1], 0.0).astype(np.float32)
    return lag


def predict_autoregressive_residual(
    residual_model: object,
    x_matrix: np.ndarray,
    seq_ids: np.ndarray,
    beta: float,
) -> np.ndarray:
    residual = np.asarray(residual_model.predict(x_matrix), dtype=np.float32)
    preds = np.empty_like(residual, dtype=np.float32)

    n = seq_ids.size
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        j = i + 1
        while j < n and seq_ids[j] == seq_ids[i]:
            j += 1

        prev = 0.0
        for k in range(i, j):
            value = (beta * prev) + float(residual[k])
            value = float(np.clip(value, -6.0, 6.0))
            preds[k] = value
            prev = value
        i = j

    return preds


def build_prediction_table(
    frame_scored: pl.DataFrame,
    pred_lgbm_t0: np.ndarray,
    pred_lgbm_t1: np.ndarray,
    pred_cat_t0: np.ndarray,
    pred_cat_t1: np.ndarray,
    pred_lgbm_ar_t1: np.ndarray,
    w_t0_lgbm: float,
    w_t1_lgbm: float,
    t1_scale: float,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    pred_ens_t0 = (w_t0_lgbm * pred_lgbm_t0) + ((1.0 - w_t0_lgbm) * pred_cat_t0)
    pred_ens_t1 = (w_t1_lgbm * pred_lgbm_t1) + ((1.0 - w_t1_lgbm) * pred_cat_t1)
    pred_ens_t1_cal = pred_ens_t1 * t1_scale

    return pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "seq_ix": frame_scored["seq_ix"].to_numpy().astype(np.int32),
            "step_in_seq": frame_scored["step_in_seq"].to_numpy().astype(np.int16),
            "t0_true": frame_scored["t0"].to_numpy().astype(np.float32),
            "t1_true": frame_scored["t1"].to_numpy().astype(np.float32),
            "t0_pred_lightgbm": pred_lgbm_t0.astype(np.float32),
            "t1_pred_lightgbm": pred_lgbm_t1.astype(np.float32),
            "t0_pred_catboost": pred_cat_t0.astype(np.float32),
            "t1_pred_catboost": pred_cat_t1.astype(np.float32),
            "t1_pred_lightgbm_ar": pred_lgbm_ar_t1.astype(np.float32),
            "t0_pred_ensemble": pred_ens_t0.astype(np.float32),
            "t1_pred_ensemble": pred_ens_t1.astype(np.float32),
            "t1_pred_ensemble_calibrated": pred_ens_t1_cal.astype(np.float32),
        }
    )


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    out_dir = Path(args.output_dir)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Load saved weights/config.
    blend_weights = json.loads((ML_MODEL_ROOT / "metrics" / "blend_weights.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    ar_cfg = json.loads((ML_MODEL_ROOT / "configs" / "t1_ar_config.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    beta_t1 = float(ar_cfg["beta_t1"])

    w_t0_lgbm = float(blend_weights["t0_lgbm_weight"])
    w_t1_lgbm = float(blend_weights["t1_primary_weight"])
    t1_scale = float(blend_weights["t1_scale"])

    # Load models.
    lgbm_t0 = joblib.load(ML_MODEL_ROOT / "models" / "lightgbm" / "model_t0.joblib")
    lgbm_t1 = joblib.load(ML_MODEL_ROOT / "models" / "lightgbm" / "model_t1.joblib")
    lgbm_t1_ar = joblib.load(ML_MODEL_ROOT / "models" / "lightgbm" / "model_t1_ar_residual.joblib")

    from catboost import CatBoostRegressor  # local import to keep startup clean

    cat_t0 = CatBoostRegressor()
    cat_t0.load_model(str(ML_MODEL_ROOT / "models" / "catboost" / "model_t0.cbm"))
    cat_t1 = CatBoostRegressor()
    cat_t1.load_model(str(ML_MODEL_ROOT / "models" / "catboost" / "model_t1.cbm"))

    feature_config = FeatureConfig()

    # Train split.
    train_raw = load_lob_frame(Path(args.train_path))
    train_scored, feat_cols = engineer_lob_features(train_raw, feature_config, only_scored_rows=True)
    train_full, _ = engineer_lob_features(train_raw, feature_config, only_scored_rows=False)

    x_train_scored = train_scored.select(feat_cols).to_numpy().astype(np.float32)
    x_train_full = train_full.select(feat_cols).to_numpy().astype(np.float32)

    train_pred_lgbm_t0 = lgbm_t0.predict(x_train_scored)
    train_pred_lgbm_t1 = lgbm_t1.predict(x_train_scored)
    train_pred_cat_t0 = cat_t0.predict(x_train_scored)
    train_pred_cat_t1 = cat_t1.predict(x_train_scored)

    seq_train_full = train_full["seq_ix"].to_numpy().astype(np.int32)
    train_ar_full = predict_autoregressive_residual(lgbm_t1_ar, x_train_full, seq_train_full, beta_t1)
    train_need_mask = train_full["need_prediction"].to_numpy().astype(bool)
    train_pred_lgbm_ar_t1 = train_ar_full[train_need_mask]

    train_table = build_prediction_table(
        frame_scored=train_scored,
        pred_lgbm_t0=np.asarray(train_pred_lgbm_t0),
        pred_lgbm_t1=np.asarray(train_pred_lgbm_t1),
        pred_cat_t0=np.asarray(train_pred_cat_t0),
        pred_cat_t1=np.asarray(train_pred_cat_t1),
        pred_lgbm_ar_t1=np.asarray(train_pred_lgbm_ar_t1),
        w_t0_lgbm=w_t0_lgbm,
        w_t1_lgbm=w_t1_lgbm,
        t1_scale=t1_scale,
    )
    train_out = out_dir / "ml_train_full.parquet"
    train_table.write_parquet(train_out)

    # Valid split.
    valid_raw = load_lob_frame(Path(args.valid_path))
    valid_scored, _ = engineer_lob_features(valid_raw, feature_config, only_scored_rows=True)
    valid_full, _ = engineer_lob_features(valid_raw, feature_config, only_scored_rows=False)

    x_valid_scored = valid_scored.select(feat_cols).to_numpy().astype(np.float32)
    x_valid_full = valid_full.select(feat_cols).to_numpy().astype(np.float32)

    valid_pred_lgbm_t0 = lgbm_t0.predict(x_valid_scored)
    valid_pred_lgbm_t1 = lgbm_t1.predict(x_valid_scored)
    valid_pred_cat_t0 = cat_t0.predict(x_valid_scored)
    valid_pred_cat_t1 = cat_t1.predict(x_valid_scored)

    seq_valid_full = valid_full["seq_ix"].to_numpy().astype(np.int32)
    valid_ar_full = predict_autoregressive_residual(lgbm_t1_ar, x_valid_full, seq_valid_full, beta_t1)
    valid_need_mask = valid_full["need_prediction"].to_numpy().astype(bool)
    valid_pred_lgbm_ar_t1 = valid_ar_full[valid_need_mask]

    valid_table = build_prediction_table(
        frame_scored=valid_scored,
        pred_lgbm_t0=np.asarray(valid_pred_lgbm_t0),
        pred_lgbm_t1=np.asarray(valid_pred_lgbm_t1),
        pred_cat_t0=np.asarray(valid_pred_cat_t0),
        pred_cat_t1=np.asarray(valid_pred_cat_t1),
        pred_lgbm_ar_t1=np.asarray(valid_pred_lgbm_ar_t1),
        w_t0_lgbm=w_t0_lgbm,
        w_t1_lgbm=w_t1_lgbm,
        t1_scale=t1_scale,
    )
    valid_out = out_dir / "ml_valid_full.parquet"
    valid_table.write_parquet(valid_out)

    # Metrics check on valid.
    scores = score_two_targets(
        valid_table["t0_true"].to_numpy(),
        valid_table["t0_pred_ensemble"].to_numpy(),
        valid_table["t1_true"].to_numpy(),
        valid_table["t1_pred_ensemble_calibrated"].to_numpy(),
    )
    (out_dir / "ml_valid_full.metrics.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(scores, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    print(f"saved_train={train_out}")
    print(f"saved_valid={valid_out}")
    print("valid_scores", json.dumps(scores, ensure_ascii=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Training Nuances for DL Models on LOB Data (v2)

> **Context:** LOB Predictorium competition -- anonymized, pre-processed LOB data.
> **Constraints:** Inference on 1 vCPU, no GPU, 16 GB RAM, 60 min for ~1500 sequences.
> **Previous version:** `Training-Nuances-LOB-v1.md`

---

## 1. Loss Function -- The Central Design Decision

### 1.1 Why Standard MSE Is Misaligned

The competition metric is the **weighted Pearson correlation** ($\rho_w$) with $w_i = |y_i|$, averaged over t0 and t1. Standard MSE is misaligned in two ways:

- MSE penalizes absolute error; the metric rewards **ranking agreement** (correlation).
- MSE weights all samples equally; the metric amplifies large price movements.

A model can achieve low MSE and poor $\rho_w$ simultaneously (e.g., predictions shifted by a constant).

### 1.2 Loss Function Options

**Option A: Weighted MSE (baseline loss).**

Aligns sample weighting with the metric. Still optimizes magnitude, not correlation. Use as a stable starting point.

**Option B: Differentiable Weighted Pearson (target loss).**

Directly optimizes the competition metric. Formula for the two heads: `loss = (1 - rho_t0) + (1 - rho_t1)`. 
*Note:* The balancing coefficient $\beta$ is **not needed** for Pearson calculation since the metric is scale-invariant (both correlations lie in `[-1, 1]`). $\beta$ is used **only** during the MSE warm-up stage.

Technical caveats & protections:

- Correlation is estimated **per batch** -- unstable at small batch sizes.
- When predictions or targets are near-constant (especially early epochs), standard deviations approach zero causing division by zero and `NaN`, permanently poisoning weights.
- **Protection:** In the denominator of the Pearson formula, replace `+ 1e-8` with a hard `torch.clamp(tgt_std, min=1e-5)` (and similarly for `pred_std`).
- **Strategy (Hard Switch):** Instead of smooth annealing, use a **Hard Switch** from MSE to Pearson.
  - Train epochs 1-5 on `Weighted MSE`. Save checkpoint.
  - Load checkpoint and train epochs 6+ on `Weighted Pearson Loss` with an updated (lowered) Learning Rate. This is safer and more predictable under strict deadlines.

**Option C: Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC).**

CCC penalizes both poor correlation and mean/scale shift. A middle ground between MSE (cares about magnitude) and Pearson (cares only about ranking). Worth experimenting with as a compromise for training stability.

**Recommendation:** Start with Weighted MSE for epochs 1-5, then Hard Switch to Weighted Pearson.

---

## 2. Multi-Target Strategy: t0 and t1

EDA established that t0 and t1 are fundamentally different signals:

| Property | t0 | t1 |
|----------|----|----|
| Lag-1 autocorrelation | 0.63 | **0.964** |
| Excess kurtosis | **23.5** | 13.2 |
| Std | 1.25 | 1.97 (1.6x wider) |
| Primary predictor | LOB features + temporal context | Own lag (temporal memory) |

### Architecture Options

**Shared backbone + separate heads (recommended).** A single CNN/RNN encoder with two independent linear projection heads. The encoder learns shared LOB representations; each head specializes on its target's characteristics. This is standard in multi-task learning and optimal for the inference budget: one forward pass produces both predictions.

**Fully separate models.** Two independent GRU/LSTM networks. Theoretically allows per-target architecture tuning (e.g., larger hidden state for t1). However, **this doubles inference compute**, which is dangerous under the 60-minute / 1 vCPU constraint for ~1500 sequences. Unless each model is very small, this path risks a Time Limit Exceeded on submission.

### Loss Balancing (Weighted MSE)

With a shared backbone and using Weighted MSE, the combined loss is:

```python
per_step_mse = mse_t0 + beta * mse_t1
```

Since t1 has 1.6x higher variance, its raw loss magnitude will dominate gradients. The $\beta$ coefficient is applied here (but *not* for Pearson loss). Options:

- Normalize targets to unit variance before loss computation.
- Tune `beta` as a hyperparameter (start with `beta = (std_t0 / std_t1)^2 ≈ 0.40`).
- Use uncertainty weighting (Kendall et al., 2018): learn `log(sigma_t0)` and `log(sigma_t1)` as trainable parameters that automatically balance task losses.

---

## 3. Loss Masking

Steps 0-98 (`need_prediction == False`) are not scored. Training on them introduces signal that is irrelevant to the competition metric.

**Instruction for Two Heads:** First, sum the losses of the two targets at each time step, and only **after that** apply the boolean mask of dimension `[batch, seq_len]` for `need_prediction == True` (steps 99-999).

```python
mask = (step_in_seq >= 99)  # shape: (batch, seq_len)
loss_t0_step = criterion(pred_t0, target_t0)
loss_t1_step = criterion(pred_t1, target_t1)
# 1. Sum losses per step
loss_step = loss_t0_step + beta * loss_t1_step  # shape: (batch, seq_len)
# 2. Apply mask
loss = (mask * loss_step).sum() / mask.sum()
```

The forward pass still runs through warm-up steps to build hidden state -- only the loss computation is masked. EDA confirmed that warm-up and prediction distributions are nearly identical, so no covariate shift is introduced by this masking.

---

## 4. Gradient Averaging and Signal Dilution

Standard `reduction='mean'` averages loss across all steps and all sequences in a batch. For LOB data this dilutes signal at two levels:

**Within-sequence dilution.** ~72% of t0 values fall in [-1, 1] (small moves, low metric weight). The remaining ~28% (large moves) dominate the competition score. Per-step averaging drowns out the informative gradients from large-move steps.

**Cross-sequence dilution.** Some sequences are more volatile (more "interesting" events). Averaging across the batch dimension dilutes their contribution.

**Solutions:**
- Weighted loss with $w = |y|$ solves within-sequence dilution by construction.
- For cross-sequence dilution: after the forward pass, re-weight each sequence's loss contribution proportionally to its mean absolute target magnitude before averaging across the batch.

The "95% noise / 5% alpha" framing (from v1) is a useful intuition but oversimplified -- every sequence contains a mix of informative and uninformative steps, and per-step weighting addresses this more precisely than sequence-level filtering.

---

## 5. Batch Size

There is no universal answer. The choice interacts with the loss function:

| Batch Size | Pros | Cons |
|------------|------|------|
| Small (16-32) | More stochasticity; may escape bad local minima | Unstable Pearson correlation estimate; poor GPU utilization |
| Medium (64-128) | Stable Pearson estimate; efficient GPU use | Moderate gradient smoothing |
| Large (256+) | Very stable statistics | Over-smooths useful noise; memory-heavy for long sequences |

**Recommendation:** 64-128. If using Pearson-based loss, do not go below 64 -- the correlation estimate over fewer than 64 sequences is statistically unreliable. Use gradient accumulation to increase effective batch size if GPU memory is a bottleneck.

---

## 6. BPTT Strategy

Full BPTT over 1000 steps creates a gradient chain of length 1000. With t0 kurtosis of 23.5, even a single volatile segment can destabilize the entire chain.

**Recommended approach: Truncated BPTT with detached hidden state.**

- The forward pass runs over the full 1000-step sequence.
- **Critical Boundary:** Do not blindly detach every 100 steps starting from 0. Accumulate memory during the warm-up (steps 0-98), and make the first `hidden.detach()` **strictly after step 98**.
- Then compute loss and gradients for intervals like 99-199, 200-299, etc. If you cut the gradient right at the 100th step (index 99), the very first predicted step ($t=99$) loses its gradient connection to the accumulated context.
- This preserves the hidden state's information (critical for t1 autocorr 0.964) while capping the gradient chain length at K.

The hidden state itself serves as a buffer for long-range memory -- truncating the gradient chain does not truncate the model's temporal memory, only the length over which credit assignment can propagate in a single backward pass.

---

## 7. Gradient Clipping and Target Clipping

### Target Clipping

99.6% of t0 and 98.4% of t1 fall within [-6, 6]. Hard-clip targets to this range during training:

```python
target = target.clamp(-6.0, 6.0)
```

For a correlation-based metric, exact prediction of extreme outliers beyond ±6 is neither feasible nor necessary. Clipping stabilizes loss magnitude and removes extreme gradient spikes from tail events.

### Gradient Clipping

Mandatory for recurrent architectures on LOB data:

```python
torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0)
```

Monitor gradient norm periodically. If it regularly exceeds 10x `max_norm`, the model is learning noise or the loss function is misconfigured.

---

## 8. Learning Rate and Scheduling

LOB data has a low signal-to-noise ratio. LR selection is critical:

- Too high: noise dominates the gradient, no convergence.
- Too low: model stalls in flat regions of the loss landscape.

**Recommendations:**

- Use **LR Range Test** (Leslie Smith) to find the optimal initial LR. Typical range for GRU on financial data: 1e-4 to 5e-3.
- **OneCycleLR** or **CosineAnnealingWarmRestarts** work well for noisy data -- they provide aggressive exploration early and fine-grained convergence late.
- If using staged loss (MSE -> Pearson), consider resetting the LR schedule when switching loss functions.

---

## 9. Regularization Stack

Gradient/target clipping stabilizes training but does not prevent overfitting. A dedicated regularization stack is required:

| Technique | Notes |
|-----------|-------|
| **Input Normalization** | **Critical:** Feeding raw volume-features (which can reach $\pm 40$) into GRU causes immediate saturation of `tanh`/`sigmoid` gates. Mandatory preprocessing: apply `sign(x) * log1p(|x|)` to all volume columns *before* feeding into the network. |
| **Variational Dropout** | Same dropout mask across all time steps within a sequence. Standard per-step dropout destroys temporal coherence of the hidden state. |
| **Weight Decay** | AdamW with `wd = 1e-4` to `1e-2`. Prefer AdamW over Adam+L2 for decoupled weight decay. |
| **Early Stopping** | Monitor weighted Pearson $\rho_w$ on validation set. Patience = 5-15 epochs. This is the single most important regularizer. |
| **Label Smoothing / Target Noise** | Add small Gaussian noise (std = 0.01-0.05) to targets during training. Mitigates overfitting to extreme kurtosis tails. |
| **Input Dropout** | Light dropout (p = 0.05-0.10) on input features. Acts as implicit data augmentation without the risks of domain-specific augmentation on pre-processed data. |

---

## 10. Instrument ID (Cluster Embedding)

Calculating the instrument cluster via the median of `p0` is a great idea from EDA, but contains a trap: if you try to compute the median and discretize it (e.g., via `np.digitize` or similar) *inside* the neural network's `forward` method, the PyTorch computational graph will break because these operations are non-differentiable and run on CPU.

**Instruction:** The calculation of `Instrument ID` must happen in the `PyTorch Dataset` class (in the `__getitem__` method), i.e., during batch preparation.

**Why this is the only correct way:**
- The model receives knowledge about the "market regime" at each of the 1000 steps.
- Gradients flow smoothly through the `Embedding` layer, allowing the network to natively learn what each cluster means (e.g., "cluster 2 is a highly volatile instrument, react stronger to OBI").
- **No data leakage:** The median is computed *only* over the allowed `warmup` period (steps 0-98).

---

## 11. State Management: Training vs. Inference

*(Carried from v1 -- this section is correct and complete.)*

There is a fundamental difference between how sequences are handled during training and during the competition's evaluation loop.

- **Training:** Mini-batches of shape `(batch_size, seq_len, n_features)`. Hidden state $h_0$ initialized to zero at the start of every sequence. No hidden state carry-over across different `seq_ix`.
- **Inference (step-by-step loop):** The scoring system feeds data row-by-row. The model must maintain and update $h_t$ manually.
  - **CRITICAL:** Track `seq_ix`. When it changes, **reset all state** (hidden state, rolling buffers) to zero. Failing to do so leaks context from a previous sequence into a new one, causing catastrophic prediction errors.

---

## 12. Hardware Setup & Hyperparameters (Local Rig)

**Target Configuration:** AMD Ryzen 7 7840H, RTX 4060 8GB, 32GB RAM.

Given this hardware, the primary bottlenecks are computational (Pearson loss complexity) and gradient stability, *not* VRAM memory capacity.

### Hardware-Specific Recommendations:

**1. RAM & Dataloaders (32GB / 8 Cores)**
- The entire dataset (~1.4GB in `float32`) easily fits in RAM.
- Use `num_workers=4` or `8` to ensure preprocessing (e.g., volume normalization and Instrument ID calculation) never starves the GPU.
- **Mandatory:** `pin_memory=True` for zero-copy transfers over the PCIe bus.

**2. VRAM Utilization (8GB RTX 4060)**
- A GRU with `hidden_size=128` (1-2 layers) + full 1000-step BPTT graph at `batch_size=128` consumes only 1.5 - 2.5 GB of VRAM. 
- **Recommendation:** Safely run `batch_size=128` to get highly stable statistical estimates for the Pearson correlation loss.

**3. Disable Mixed Precision (AMP)**
- **Critical:** Do *not* use FP16. The Pearson correlation formula requires calculating variances and squared sums. In `float16` (max value 65504), this leads to instantaneous overflow (`Inf`) or underflow (`NaN`) on flat batches.
- Since VRAM is abundant, run in pure `float32` to guarantee gradient stability across 1000 recurrent steps.

**4. `torch.compile` Acceleration**
- The RTX 4060 (Ada Lovelace architecture) is highly optimized for PyTorch 2.x compilation.
- Add `model = torch.compile(model)` before the training loop for a "free" 15-30% speed boost. *(Note: If `torch.compile` conflicts with CuDNN GRU implementations, try `backend="aot_eager"` or compile only the loss function).*

---

## 13. Summary: Training Configuration Checklist

```
[ ] Loss: Weighted MSE baseline -> Hard Switch to Weighted Pearson
[ ] Architecture: shared backbone + 2 separate heads for t0/t1
[ ] Loss balancing: beta weighting for MSE, formula for Pearson
[ ] Loss masking: sum per-step losses first, then mask steps 0-98
[ ] Target clipping: [-6, 6]
[ ] BPTT: truncated (first detach strictly after step 98)

# Terminal Guidelines

- Prefer non-interactive execution. Don’t rely on pagers/editors/prompts.
  - Disable pagers per-command (don’t export globally): `PAGER=cat <cmd>`; `git --no-pager <cmd>`

- Limit output intentionally.
  - Prefer command-native limits (e.g., `git log -n N`, `journalctl -n N --no-pager`).
  - Errors/debug: prefer last lines (`tail -n N`). Help/headers: first lines (`head -n N`).
  - `rg -m N` limits matches; use `-A/-B/-C` for context.

- Pipelines may buffer output (non-TTY). If real-time matters:
  - `stdbuf -oL -eL <cmd> | ...` (if available) or `grep --line-buffered ...`
  - Python: `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` / `python -u`

- Streams must be bounded.
  - Snapshot then bounded follow: `tail -n N ...`; `journalctl -n N --no-pager`; `timeout 10s tail -F ...`
  - Use `timeout` only for observation/reading, not for side-effecting operations.

- Prefer stable output when supported: `--json`, `--porcelain`, `--quiet`, `--color=never` (don’t guess flags).

- Don’t blanket-use `set -euo pipefail`. Use strict mode only in controlled scripts with explicit handling of expected non-zero exits (grep/diff/test).
```

# Terminal Guidelines

- Prefer non-interactive execution. Don’t rely on pagers/editors/prompts.
  - Disable pagers per-command (don’t export globally): `PAGER=cat <cmd>`; `git --no-pager <cmd>`

- Limit output intentionally.
  - Prefer command-native limits (e.g., `git log -n N`, `journalctl -n N --no-pager`).
  - Errors/debug: prefer last lines (`tail -n N`). Help/headers: first lines (`head -n N`).
  - `rg -m N` limits matches; use `-A/-B/-C` for context.

- Pipelines may buffer output (non-TTY). If real-time matters:
  - `stdbuf -oL -eL <cmd> | ...` (if available) or `grep --line-buffered ...`
  - Python: `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` / `python -u`

- Streams must be bounded.
  - Snapshot then bounded follow: `tail -n N ...`; `journalctl -n N --no-pager`; `timeout 10s tail -F ...`
  - Use `timeout` only for observation/reading, not for side-effecting operations.

- Prefer stable output when supported: `--json`, `--porcelain`, `--quiet`, `--color=never` (don’t guess flags).

- Don’t blanket-use `set -euo pipefail`. Use strict mode only in controlled scripts with explicit handling of expected non-zero exits (grep/diff/test).

## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and file path so you can open the source for full instructions when using a specific skill.
### Available skills

{"cmd":"/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-Predictorium/.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path

train_path = Path('/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_train_full.parquet')
valid_path = Path('/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_valid_full.parquet')

def wpc(y, p):
    y = np.asarray(y, np.float64)
    p = np.clip(np.asarray(p, np.float64), -6, 6)
    w = np.maximum(np.abs(y), 1e-8)
    sw = w.sum()
    ym = (w*y).sum()/sw
    pm = (w*p).sum()/sw
    yc=y-ym; pc=p-pm
    cov=(w*yc*pc).sum()/sw
    vy=(w*yc*yc).sum()/sw
    vp=(w*pc*pc).sum()/sw
    if vy<=0 or vp<=0: return 0.0
    return float(cov/np.sqrt(vy*vp))

def score(df, t0, t1):
    m = df['need_prediction'].to_numpy().astype(bool)
    y0 = df['t0_true'].to_numpy()[m]
    y1 = df['t1_true'].to_numpy()[m]
    p0 = np.asarray(t0)[m]
    p1 = np.asarray(t1)[m]
    s0 = wpc(y0,p0); s1 = wpc(y1,p1)
    return s0,s1,(s0+s1)/2

tr = pd.read_parquet(train_path)
va = pd.read_parquet(valid_path)

# baseline
b0,b1,br = score(va, va.t0_pred_vendor.values, va.t1_pred_vendor.values)
print('baseline valid', b0,b1,br)

# seq indices split
for df in (tr,va):
    df.sort_values(['seq_ix','step_in_seq'], inplace=True)

def apply_alpha(df, alpha0, alpha1):
    p0 = df['t0_pred_vendor'].to_numpy().astype(np.float64)
    p1 = df['t1_pred_vendor'].to_numpy().astype(np.float64)
    seq = df['seq_ix'].to_numpy()
    out0 = np.empty_like(p0)
    out1 = np.empty_like(p1)
    prev0 = 0.0
    prev1 = 0.0
    prev_seq = None
    for i in range(len(df)):
        s = seq[i]
        if prev_seq is None or s != prev_seq:
            prev0 = p0[i]
            prev1 = p1[i]
        else:
            prev0 = alpha0*prev0 + (1-alpha0)*p0[i]
            prev1 = alpha1*prev1 + (1-alpha1)*p1[i]
        out0[i] = prev0
        out1[i] = prev1
        prev_seq = s
    return out0, out1

best = None
for a0 in np.linspace(0,0.98,25):
    for a1 in np.linspace(0,0.995,60):
        p0,p1 = apply_alpha(tr,a0,a1)
        _,_,sr = score(tr,p0,p1)
        if best is None or sr>best[0]:
            best=(sr,a0,a1)
print('best alpha train',best)

# evaluate top train alphas on valid
cands=[]
for a0 in np.linspace(0,0.98,25):
    for a1 in np.linspace(0,0.995,60):
        p0,p1 = apply_alpha(tr,a0,a1)
        _,_,sr = score(tr,p0,p1)
        cands.append((sr,a0,a1))
cands.sort(reverse=True)
for rank,(_,a0,a1) in enumerate(cands[:20],1):
    p0,p1 = apply_alpha(va,a0,a1)
    s0,s1,sr = score(va,p0,p1)
    print(rank,'a0',round(a0,4),'a1',round(a1,4),'valid',round(s0,6),round(s1,6),round(sr,6))

# direct valid-opt alpha (for reference only)
bv=None
for a0 in np.linspace(0,0.98,61):
    for a1 in np.linspace(0,0.995,120):
        p0,p1=apply_alpha(va,a0,a1)
        s0,s1,sr=score(va,p0,p1)
        if bv is None or sr>bv[0]:
            bv=(sr,a0,a1,s0,s1)
print('oracle valid alpha',bv)

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path

train_path = Path('/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_train_full.parquet')
valid_path = Path('/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_valid_full.parquet')

def wpc(y, p):
    y = np.asarray(y, np.float64)
    p = np.clip(np.asarray(p, np.float64), -6, 6)
    w = np.maximum(np.abs(y), 1e-8)
    sw = w.sum()
    ym = (w*y).sum()/sw
    pm = (w*p).sum()/sw
    yc=y-ym; pc=p-pm
    cov=(w*yc*pc).sum()/sw
    vy=(w*yc*yc).sum()/sw
    vp=(w*pc*pc).sum()/sw
    if vy<=0 or vp<=0: return 0.0
    return float(cov/np.sqrt(vy*vp))

def score(df, t0, t1):
    m = df['need_prediction'].to_numpy().astype(bool)
    y0 = df['t0_true'].to_numpy()[m]
    y1 = df['t1_true'].to_numpy()[m]
    p0 = np.asarray(t0)[m]
    p1 = np.asarray(t1)[m]
    s0 = wpc(y0,p0); s1 = wpc(y1,p1)
    return s0,s1,(s0+s1)/2

tr = pd.read_parquet(train_path).sort_values(['seq_ix','step_in_seq'])
va = pd.read_parquet(valid_path).sort_values(['seq_ix','step_in_seq'])

def apply_alpha(df, alpha0, alpha1):
    p0 = df['t0_pred_vendor'].to_numpy().astype(np.float64)
    p1 = df['t1_pred_vendor'].to_numpy().astype(np.float64)
    seq = df['seq_ix'].to_numpy()
    out0 = np.empty_like(p0)
    out1 = np.empty_like(p1)
    prev0 = p0[0]
    prev1 = p1[0]
    prev_seq = seq[0]
    out0[0]=prev0; out1[0]=prev1
    for i in range(1,len(df)):
        s = seq[i]
        if s != prev_seq:
            prev0 = p0[i]
            prev1 = p1[i]
        else:
            prev0 = alpha0*prev0 + (1-alpha0)*p0[i]
            prev1 = alpha1*prev1 + (1-alpha1)*p1[i]
        out0[i] = prev0
        out1[i] = prev1
        prev_seq = s
    return out0, out1

b0,b1,br = score(va, va.t0_pred_vendor.values, va.t1_pred_vendor.values)
print('baseline valid', round(b0,6), round(b1,6), round(br,6))

alphas0 = [0.0,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.85,0.92,0.97]
alphas1 = [0.0,0.5,0.7,0.85,0.92,0.97,0.985,0.995]

best_train = (-1,None,None)
for a0 in alphas0:
    for a1 in alphas1:
        p0,p1 = apply_alpha(tr,a0,a1)
        _,_,r = score(tr,p0,p1)
        if r>best_train[0]:
            best_train=(r,a0,a1)
print('best train grid', best_train)

print('valid grid:')
best_valid=(-1,None,None,None,None)
for a0 in alphas0:
    for a1 in alphas1:
        p0,p1=apply_alpha(va,a0,a1)
        s0,s1,r=score(va,p0,p1)
        print(f'a0={a0:.3f} a1={a1:.3f} -> t0={s0:.6f} t1={s1:.6f} rho={r:.6f}')
        if r>best_valid[0]:
            best_valid=(r,a0,a1,s0,s1)
print('best valid grid', best_valid)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
from numba import njit

train_path = Path('/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_train_full.parquet')
valid_path = Path('/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_valid_full.parquet')

@njit
def apply_alpha_seq(pred, seq, alpha):
    out = np.empty_like(pred)
    out[0] = pred[0]
    prev = pred[0]
    prev_seq = seq[0]
    for i in range(1, pred.shape[0]):
        s = seq[i]
        if s != prev_seq:
            prev = pred[i]
        else:
            prev = alpha * prev + (1.0 - alpha) * pred[i]
        out[i] = prev
        prev_seq = s
    return out

@njit
def weighted_pearson(y, p):
    n = y.shape[0]
    sum_w = 0.0
    sum_wy = 0.0
    sum_wp = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        w = abs(y[i])
        if w < 1e-8:
            w = 1e-8
        pv = p[i]
        if pv < -6.0:
            pv = -6.0
        elif pv > 6.0:
            pv = 6.0
        sum_w += w
        sum_wy += w * y[i]
        sum_wp += w * pv
    my = sum_wy / sum_w
    mp = sum_wp / sum_w

    cov = 0.0
    vy = 0.0
    vp = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        w = abs(y[i])
        if w < 1e-8:
            w = 1e-8
        pv = p[i]
        if pv < -6.0:
            pv = -6.0
        elif pv > 6.0:
            pv = 6.0
        dy = y[i] - my
        dp = pv - mp
        cov += w * dy * dp
        vy += w * dy * dy
        vp += w * dp * dp
    cov /= sum_w
    vy /= sum_w
    vp /= sum_w
    if vy <= 0.0 or vp <= 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return cov / np.sqrt(vy * vp)

@njit
def find_best_alpha(y0, y1, p0, p1, seq, mask, alphas0, alphas1):
    best = -1e9
    best_a0 = 0.0
    best_a1 = 0.0
    # pre-alloc buffers
    pred0 = np.empty_like(p0)
    pred1 = np.empty_like(p1)
    y0m = y0[mask]
    y1m = y1[mask]

    for i in range(alphas0.shape[0]):
        a0 = alphas0[i]
        pred0 = apply_alpha_seq(p0, seq, a0)
        pred0m = pred0[mask]
        s0 = weighted_pearson(y0m, pred0m)
        for j in range(alphas1.shape[0]):
            a1 = alphas1[j]
            pred1 = apply_alpha_seq(p1, seq, a1)
            pred1m = pred1[mask]
            s1 = weighted_pearson(y1m, pred1m)
            s = 0.5 * (s0 + s1)
            if s > best:
                best = s
                best_a0 = a0
                best_a1 = a1
    return best, best_a0, best_a1

@njit
def score_at(y0, y1, p0, p1, seq, mask, a0, a1):
    pred0 = apply_alpha_seq(p0, seq, a0)
    pred1 = apply_alpha_seq(p1, seq, a1)
    y0m = y0[mask]
    y1m = y1[mask]
    p0m = pred0[mask]
    p1m = pred1[mask]
    s0 = weighted_pearson(y0m, p0m)
    s1 = weighted_pearson(y1m, p1m)
    return s0, s1, 0.5*(s0+s1)


def load(path):
    df = pd.read_parquet(path).sort_values(['seq_ix','step_in_seq'])
    return {
        'seq': df['seq_ix'].to_numpy(np.int32),
        'mask': df['need_prediction'].to_numpy(bool),
        'y0': df['t0_true'].to_numpy(np.float32),
        'y1': df['t1_true'].to_numpy(np.float32),
        'p0': df['t0_pred_vendor'].to_numpy(np.float32),
        'p1': df['t1_pred_vendor'].to_numpy(np.float32),
    }

train = load(train_path)
valid = load(valid_path)

# compile
_ = score_at(valid['y0'], valid['y1'], valid['p0'], valid['p1'], valid['seq'], valid['mask'], 0.0, 0.0)

b = score_at(valid['y0'], valid['y1'], valid['p0'], valid['p1'], valid['seq'], valid['mask'], 0.0, 0.0)
print('baseline valid', tuple(round(float(x), 6) for x in b))

alphas0 = np.linspace(0.0, 0.95, 11).astype(np.float32)
alphas1 = np.linspace(0.0, 0.995, 11).astype(np.float32)

best_train = find_best_alpha(train['y0'], train['y1'], train['p0'], train['p1'], train['seq'], train['mask'], alphas0, alphas1)
print('best coarse train', tuple(float(x) for x in best_train))

a0 = float(best_train[1])
a1 = float(best_train[2])

# local refinement near train optimum
low0 = max(0.0, a0 - 0.18)
hi0 = min(0.99, a0 + 0.18)
low1 = max(0.0, a1 - 0.18)
hi1 = min(0.999, a1 + 0.18)
ref0 = np.linspace(low0, hi0, 13).astype(np.float32)
ref1 = np.linspace(low1, hi1, 13).astype(np.float32)

best_train_ref = find_best_alpha(train['y0'], train['y1'], train['p0'], train['p1'], train['seq'], train['mask'], ref0, ref1)
print('best refined train', tuple(float(x) for x in best_train_ref))

sv = score_at(valid['y0'], valid['y1'], valid['p0'], valid['p1'], valid['seq'], valid['mask'], float(best_train_ref[1]), float(best_train_ref[2]))
print('valid @train-opt', tuple(round(float(x), 6) for x in sv))

# reference: valid-opt over same refined grid (not honest)
best_valid_ref = find_best_alpha(valid['y0'], valid['y1'], valid['p0'], valid['p1'], valid['seq'], valid['mask'], ref0, ref1)
print('best refined valid (oracle)', tuple(float(x) for x in best_valid_ref))
sv_oracle = score_at(valid['y0'], valid['y1'], valid['p0'], valid['p1'], valid['seq'], valid['mask'], float(best_valid_ref[1]), float(best_valid_ref[2]))
print('valid @valid-opt', tuple(round(float(x), 6) for x in sv_oracle))

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
from numba import njit

train_path = Path('/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_train_full.parquet')
valid_path = Path('/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_valid_full.parquet')

@njit
def apply_alpha_seq(pred, seq, alpha):
    out = np.empty_like(pred)
    # initialize from first non-nan if needed
    first = pred[0]
    if first != first:
        first = 0.0
    out[0] = first
    prev = first
    prev_seq = seq[0]
    for i in range(1, pred.shape[0]):
        s = seq[i]
        v = pred[i]
        if v != v:
            v = prev
        if s != prev_seq:
            prev = v
        else:
            prev = alpha * prev + (1.0 - alpha) * v
        out[i] = prev
        prev_seq = s
    return out

@njit
def weighted_pearson(y, p):
    n = y.shape[0]
    sum_w = 0.0
    sum_wy = 0.0
    sum_wp = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        w = abs(y[i])
        if w < 1e-8:
            w = 1e-8
        pv = p[i]
        if pv < -6.0:
            pv = -6.0
        elif pv > 6.0:
            pv = 6.0
        sum_w += w
        sum_wy += w * y[i]
        sum_wp += w * pv
    my = sum_wy / sum_w
    mp = sum_wp / sum_w

    cov = 0.0
    vy = 0.0
    vp = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        w = abs(y[i])
        if w < 1e-8:
            w = 1e-8
        pv = p[i]
        if pv < -6.0:
            pv = -6.0
        elif pv > 6.0:
            pv = 6.0
        dy = y[i] - my
        dp = pv - mp
        cov += w * dy * dp
        vy += w * dy * dy
        vp += w * dp * dp
    cov /= sum_w
    vy /= sum_w
    vp /= sum_w
    if vy <= 0.0 or vp <= 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return cov / np.sqrt(vy * vp)

@njit
def find_best_alpha(y0, y1, p0, p1, seq, mask, alphas0, alphas1):
    best = -1e9
    best_a0 = 0.0
    best_a1 = 0.0
    y0m = y0[mask]
    y1m = y1[mask]
    pred1_cache = []

    for i in range(alphas0.shape[0]):
        a0 = alphas0[i]
        pred0 = apply_alpha_seq(p0, seq, a0)
        s0 = weighted_pearson(y0m, pred0[mask])
        for j in range(alphas1.shape[0]):
            a1 = alphas1[j]
            pred1 = apply_alpha_seq(p1, seq, a1)
            s1 = weighted_pearson(y1m, pred1[mask])
            s = 0.5 * (s0 + s1)
            if s > best:
                best = s
                best_a0 = a0
                best_a1 = a1
    return best, best_a0, best_a1

@njit
def score_at(y0, y1, p0, p1, seq, mask, a0, a1):
    pred0 = apply_alpha_seq(p0, seq, a0)
    pred1 = apply_alpha_seq(p1, seq, a1)
    y0m = y0[mask]
    y1m = y1[mask]
    p0m = pred0[mask]
    p1m = pred1[mask]
    s0 = weighted_pearson(y0m, p0m)
    s1 = weighted_pearson(y1m, p1m)
    return s0, s1, 0.5*(s0+s1)


def load(path):
    df = pd.read_parquet(path).sort_values(['seq_ix','step_in_seq'])
    return {
        'seq': df['seq_ix'].to_numpy(np.int32),
        'mask': df['need_prediction'].to_numpy(bool),
        'y0': df['t0_true'].to_numpy(np.float32),
        'y1': df['t1_true'].to_numpy(np.float32),
        'p0': df['t0_pred_vendor'].to_numpy(np.float32),
        'p1': df['t1_pred_vendor'].to_numpy(np.float32),
    }

train = load(train_path)
valid = load(valid_path)

_ = score_at(valid['y0'], valid['y1'], valid['p0'], valid['p1'], valid['seq'], valid['mask'], 0.0, 0.0)

b = score_at(valid['y0'], valid['y1'], valid['p0'], valid['p1'], valid['seq'], valid['mask'], 0.0, 0.0)
print('baseline valid', tuple(round(float(x), 6) for x in b))

alphas0 = np.linspace(0.0, 0.95, 11).astype(np.float32)
alphas1 = np.linspace(0.0, 0.995, 11).astype(np.float32)

best_train = find_best_alpha(train['y0'], train['y1'], train['p0'], train['p1'], train['seq'], train['mask'], alphas0, alphas1)
print('best coarse train', tuple(float(x) for x in best_train))

a0 = float(best_train[1])
a1 = float(best_train[2])
low0 = max(0.0, a0 - 0.18)
hi0 = min(0.99, a0 + 0.18)
low1 = max(0.0, a1 - 0.18)
hi1 = min(0.999, a1 + 0.18)
ref0 = np.linspace(low0, hi0, 13).astype(np.float32)
ref1 = np.linspace(low1, hi1, 13).astype(np.float32)

print('best refined train', tuple(float(x) for x in best_train_ref))

sv = score_at(valid['y0'], valid['y1'], valid['p0'], valid['p1'], valid['seq'], valid['mask'], float(best_train_ref[1]), float(best_train_ref[2]))
print('valid @train-opt', tuple(round(float(x), 6) for x in sv))

best_valid_ref = find_best_alpha(valid['y0'], valid['y1'], valid['p0'], valid['p1'], valid['seq'], valid['mask'], ref0, ref1)
print('best refined valid (oracle)', tuple(float(x) for x in best_valid_ref))

print('valid @valid-opt', tuple(round(float(x), 6) for x in sv_oracle))

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
from numba import njit

train_path = Path('/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_train_full.parquet')
valid_path = Path('/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_valid_full.parquet')

@njit
def apply_alpha_seq(pred, seq, alpha):
    out = np.empty_like(pred)
    first = pred[0]
    if first != first:
        first = 0.0
    out[0] = first
    prev = first
    prev_seq = seq[0]
    for i in range(1, pred.shape[0]):
        s = seq[i]
        v = pred[i]
        if v != v:
            v = prev
        if s != prev_seq:
            prev = v
        else:
            prev = alpha * prev + (1.0 - alpha) * v
        out[i] = prev
        prev_seq = s
    return out

@njit
def weighted_pearson(y, p):
    n = y.shape[0]
    sum_w = 0.0
    sum_wy = 0.0
    sum_wp = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        w = abs(y[i])
        if w < 1e-8:
            w = 1e-8
        pv = p[i]
        if pv < -6.0:
            pv = -6.0
        elif pv > 6.0:
            pv = 6.0
        sum_w += w
        sum_wy += w * y[i]
        sum_wp += w * pv
    my = sum_wy / sum_w
    mp = sum_wp / sum_w

    cov = 0.0
    vy = 0.0
    vp = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        w = abs(y[i])
        if w < 1e-8:
            w = 1e-8
        pv = p[i]
        if pv < -6.0:
            pv = -6.0
        elif pv > 6.0:
            pv = 6.0
        dy = y[i] - my
        dp = pv - mp
        cov += w * dy * dp
        vy += w * dy * dy
        vp += w * dp * dp
    cov /= sum_w
    vy /= sum_w
    vp /= sum_w
    if vy <= 0.0 or vp <= 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return cov / np.sqrt(vy * vp)

@njit
def find_best_alpha(y0, y1, p0, p1, seq, mask, alphas0, alphas1):
    best = -1e9
    best_a0 = 0.0
    best_a1 = 0.0
    y0m = y0[mask]
    y1m = y1[mask]

    for i in range(alphas0.shape[0]):
        a0 = alphas0[i]
        pred0 = apply_alpha_seq(p0, seq, a0)
        s0 = weighted_pearson(y0m, pred0[mask])
        for j in range(alphas1.shape[0]):
            a1 = alphas1[j]
            pred1 = apply_alpha_seq(p1, seq, a1)
            s1 = weighted_pearson(y1m, pred1[mask])
            s = 0.5 * (s0 + s1)
            if s > best:
                best = s
                best_a0 = a0
                best_a1 = a1
    return best, best_a0, best_a1

@njit
def score_at(y0, y1, p0, p1, seq, mask, a0, a1):
    pred0 = apply_alpha_seq(p0, seq, a0)
    pred1 = apply_alpha_seq(p1, seq, a1)
    y0m = y0[mask]
    y1m = y1[mask]
    p0m = pred0[mask]
    p1m = pred1[mask]
    s0 = weighted_pearson(y0m, p0m)
    s1 = weighted_pearson(y1m, p1m)
    return s0, s1, 0.5*(s0+s1)

    df = pd.read_parquet(path).sort_values(['seq_ix','step_in_seq'])

alphas1 = np.linspace(0.0, 0.995, 11).astype(np.float32)

hi0 = min(0.99, a0 + 0.18)

print('valid @valid-opt', tuple(round(float(x), 6) for x in sv_oracle))

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def wpc(y,p):
    y=np.asarray(y,np.float64); p=np.clip(np.asarray(p,np.float64),-6,6)
    w=np.maximum(np.abs(y),1e-8); sw=w.sum();
    ym=(w*y).sum()/sw; pm=(w*p).sum()/sw
    yc=y-ym; pc=p-pm
    cov=(w*yc*pc).sum()/sw; vy=(w*yc*yc).sum()/sw; vp=(w*pc*pc).sum()/sw
    return 0.0 if vy<=0 or vp<=0 else float(cov/np.sqrt(vy*vp))

def score(df,p0,p1):
    m=df.need_prediction.values
    y0=df.t0_true.values[m]; y1=df.t1_true.values[m]
    s0=wpc(y0,p0[m]); s1=wpc(y1,p1[m]); return s0,s1,(s0+s1)/2

for path in ['/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_valid_full.parquet','/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_train_full.parquet']:
    df=pd.read_parquet(path).sort_values(['seq_ix','step_in_seq'])
    base0=df.t0_pred_vendor.fillna(0).values.astype(np.float32)
    base1=df.t1_pred_vendor.fillna(0).values.astype(np.float32)
    seq=df.seq_ix.values
    print('\n',path)
    print('baseline',score(df,base0,base1))
    for sh in [-5,-3,-2,-1,1,2,3,5]:
        p0=np.empty_like(base0); p1=np.empty_like(base1)
        p0[:] = 0; p1[:] = 0
        # shift within seq
        i=0; n=len(df)
        while i<n:
            j=i+1
            while j<n and seq[j]==seq[i]:
                j+=1
            x0=base0[i:j]; x1=base1[i:j]
            if sh>0:
                p0[i+sh:j]=x0[:(j-i-sh)]
                p1[i+sh:j]=x1[:(j-i-sh)]
                p0[i:i+sh]=x0[0]
                p1[i:i+sh]=x1[0]
            else:
                k=-sh
                p0[i:j-k]=x0[k:]
                p1[i:j-k]=x1[k:]
                p0[j-k:j]=x0[-1]
                p1[j-k:j]=x1[-1]
            i=j
        s=score(df,p0,p1)
        print('shift',sh,s)

{"cmd":"/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-Predictorium/.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge

train_path = Path('/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_train_full.parquet')
valid_path = Path('/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/vendor_valid_full.parquet')

def wpc(y,p):
    y=np.asarray(y,np.float64); p=np.clip(np.asarray(p,np.float64),-6,6)
    w=np.maximum(np.abs(y),1e-8); sw=w.sum()
    ym=(w*y).sum()/sw; pm=(w*p).sum()/sw
    yc=y-ym; pc=p-pm
    cov=(w*yc*pc).sum()/sw; vy=(w*yc*yc).sum()/sw; vp=(w*pc*pc).sum()/sw
    return 0.0 if vy<=0 or vp<=0 else float(cov/np.sqrt(vy*vp))

def score(df,p0,p1):
    m=df.need_prediction.values.astype(bool)
    y0=df.t0_true.values[m]; y1=df.t1_true.values[m]
    s0=wpc(y0,p0[m]); s1=wpc(y1,p1[m])
    return s0,s1,(s0+s1)/2

def add_lags(df, col, lags=(1,2,3,5)):
    seq=df.seq_ix.values
    arr=df[col].fillna(0).values.astype(np.float32)
    out={f'{col}_lag{l}':np.zeros_like(arr) for l in lags}
    for l in lags:
        lag=out[f'{col}_lag{l}']
        lag[:]=arr
        for i in range(len(arr)):
            j=i-l
            if j>=0 and seq[j]==seq[i]:
                lag[i]=arr[j]
            elif j>=0 and seq[j]!=seq[i]:
                lag[i]=arr[i]
            elif j<0:
                lag[i]=arr[i]
    return out

tr=pd.read_parquet(train_path).sort_values(['seq_ix','step_in_seq'])
va=pd.read_parquet(valid_path).sort_values(['seq_ix','step_in_seq'])

base0=va.t0_pred_vendor.fillna(0).values
base1=va.t1_pred_vendor.fillna(0).values
print('baseline valid',score(va,base0,base1))

# Feature matrix for t1 meta-predictor
for df in (tr,va):
    l1=add_lags(df,'t1_pred_vendor',(1,2,3,4,5))
    l0=add_lags(df,'t0_pred_vendor',(1,2,3))
    for k,v in {**l1,**l0}.items():
        df[k]=v
    x_cols=[
        't1_pred_vendor','t1_pred_vendor_lag1','t1_pred_vendor_lag2','t1_pred_vendor_lag3','t1_pred_vendor_lag4','t1_pred_vendor_lag5',
        't0_pred_vendor','t0_pred_vendor_lag1','t0_pred_vendor_lag2','t0_pred_vendor_lag3',
    ]
    # derivative-like
    df['d1']=df['t1_pred_vendor']-df['t1_pred_vendor_lag1']
    df['d2']=df['t1_pred_vendor_lag1']-df['t1_pred_vendor_lag2']
    df['d3']=df['t1_pred_vendor_lag2']-df['t1_pred_vendor_lag3']
    df['d0']=df['t0_pred_vendor']-df['t0_pred_vendor_lag1']
    x_cols += ['d1','d2','d3','d0']

mtr=tr.need_prediction.values.astype(bool)
mva=va.need_prediction.values.astype(bool)

x_cols=[c for c in tr.columns if c.startswith('t1_pred_vendor') or c.startswith('t0_pred_vendor') or c in ['d1','d2','d3','d0']]
Xtr=tr.loc[mtr,x_cols].fillna(0).values.astype(np.float32)
ytr=tr.loc[mtr,'t1_true'].values.astype(np.float32)
Xva=va.loc[mva,x_cols].fillna(0).values.astype(np.float32)

for alpha in [0.0,1e-4,1e-3,1e-2,1e-1,1.0,3.0,10.0]:
    model=Ridge(alpha=alpha,fit_intercept=True,random_state=42)
    model.fit(Xtr,ytr)
    p1=np.zeros(len(va),dtype=np.float32)
    p1[mva]=model.predict(Xva).astype(np.float32)

    # optionally blend with raw vendor t1
    raw1=va.t1_pred_vendor.fillna(0).values.astype(np.float32)
    raw0=va.t0_pred_vendor.fillna(0).values.astype(np.float32)
    for w in [0.0,0.1,0.2,0.35,0.5,0.65,0.8,1.0]:
        p1b=(1-w)*raw1 + w*p1
        s=score(va,raw0,p1b)
        print(f'alpha={alpha:<5} w={w:<4} -> t0={s[0]:.6f} t1={s[1]:.6f} rho={s[2]:.6f}')

# simple lead filter scan (causal)
raw1=va.t1_pred_vendor.fillna(0).values.astype(np.float32)
seq=va.seq_ix.values
lag1=np.copy(raw1)
for i in range(1,len(raw1)):
    if seq[i]==seq[i-1]: lag1[i]=raw1[i-1]

delta=raw1-lag1
best=None
for g in np.linspace(-2.0,4.0,61):
    p1=raw1 + g*delta
    s=score(va,va.t0_pred_vendor.fillna(0).values,p1)
    if best is None or s[2]>best[0]:
        best=(s[2],g,s)
print('best simple lead on valid (oracle)',best)

- собрать таблицу результатов;
- выбрать лучшую модель;
- если пороги не достигнуты, сделать ещё 1-2 целевых прогона только от лучшей ветки.

# Welcome to the Wunder Challenge 2!
2025-12-30

We're excited to have you here. This is a machine learning competition where you'll build a model to predict future price movements based on Limit Order Book (LOB) data and recent trades. It’s a challenging sequence modeling problem from the domain of high-frequency trading. Let's get started!

## Your mission

Your goal is to predict two target variables (**t0** and **t1**) which represent two different types of future price movements. You will make these predictions based on the sequence of market states (LOB and trades) that came before. You'll be given the market's history up to a certain point, and you need to forecast these future indicators.

## How it works

The dataset is a single table in Parquet format, containing multiple independent sequences. Here’s what you need to know.

### The data format

Each row in the table represents a single market state at a specific step in a sequence. The table has the following columns:

*   `seq_ix`: An ID for the sequence. When this number changes, you're starting a new, completely independent sequence.
*   `step_in_seq`: The step number within a sequence (from 0 to 999).
*   `need_prediction`: A boolean that’s `True` if we need a prediction from you for this step, and `False` otherwise.

**Feature Columns:**
The numeric features provide a structured representation of the market state, derived from the Limit Order Book (LOB) and recent trade activity. While the data is anonymized, the structure follows standard market data conventions:

*   `p0`...`p5`: **Bid Price Features**. Anonymized features derived from the bid side of the Limit Order Book representing prices at different levels.
*   `p6`...`p11`: **Ask Price Features**. Anonymized features derived from the ask side of the Limit Order Book representing prices at different levels.
*   `v0`...`v5`: **Bid Volume Features**. Anonymized features representing volumes corresponding to price levels on the bid side.
*   `v6`...`v11`: **Ask Volume Features**. Anonymized features representing volumes corresponding to price levels on the ask side.
*   `dp0`...`dp3`: **Trade Price Features**. Anonymized features representing trade prices (derived from both bid and ask trades).
*   `dv0`...`dv3`: **Trade Volume Features**. Anonymized features representing trade volumes (derived from both bid and ask trades).

**Target Columns:**
*   `t0`, `t1`: The targets represent two different types of future price movement indicators derived from the market state. These values are also anonymized. Your task is to predict these values.

### The sequences

Each sequence is exactly **1000 steps** long.

> **Note:**
> The first 99 steps (0-98) of every sequence are for warm-up. Your model can use them to build context, but we won't score your predictions here. Your score comes from predictions for the remaining 901 steps (steps 99 to 999).

Because each sequence is independent, you must reset your model’s internal state whenever you see a new `seq_ix`.

You can also rely on two key facts about the data ordering:
*   **Within a sequence**, all steps are ordered by time.
*   **The sequences themselves** are randomly shuffled, so `seq_ix` and `seq_ix + 1` are not related.

> **Tip: How to create a validation set**
> We provide a dedicated `valid.parquet` file which you can use to test your model's performance. However, since all sequences are independent, you are not limited to this split. You can combine the datasets and create your own custom cross-validation strategy (e.g., K-Fold split by `seq_ix`) to potentially get more robust estimates.

## Evaluation and metrics

We'll evaluate your predictions using the **Weighted Pearson Correlation Coefficient** score.

The metric emphasizes performance on data points with larger target amplitudes (larger price movements). Specifically:
*   Predictions are clipped to the range [-6, 6] to handle outliers.
*   The correlation is weighted by the absolute value of the target (amplitude of price change).
*   Implementation details can be found in `utils.weighted_pearson_correlation`.

For each target *i* (where i is t0, t1), the score is calculated as the Weighted Pearson correlation between the true values and your predictions.

The final score is the average of the correlation scores across the two targets.

A higher correlation score is better!

## 🚀 Quick start

The fastest way to get started is to run the **Vanilla GRU baseline example** solution we've provided. This solution was generated by an LLM as a demonstration. This will help you understand the data flow and submission format.

```bash
# Navigate to the example directory
cd example_solution

# Run the baseline solution
python solution.py
```

For a full walkthrough, including setting up your Python environment, check out our detailed Quick Start Guide in `docs/quick_start.md`.

After running the example, you'll be ready to build your own model. The provided solution is just a basic placeholder—the real fun is creating something more powerful!

> **Tip: What models could work?**
> Since this is a sequence modeling task, you could explore:
> *   Recurrent models like **LSTM** or **GRU**.
> *   Attention-based models like the **Transformer**.
> *   Newer architectures like **Mamba-2**.

## How to submit your solution

Your submission must be a `.zip` file containing a `solution.py` file.

### Required structure

Your `solution.py` must define a class named `PredictionModel`. This class must have a `predict` method with the following signature:

```python
import numpy as np
from utils import DataPoint

class PredictionModel:
    def __init__(self):
        # Initialize your model, internal state, etc.
        pass

    def predict(self, data_point: DataPoint) -> np.ndarray | None:
        # Your logic here.
        if not data_point.need_prediction:
            return None

        # When a prediction is needed, return a numpy array of length 2 (for t0 and t1).
        prediction = np.zeros(2) # Replace with your model's output
        return prediction
```

The `data_point` object passed to your `predict` method is an instance of the `DataPoint` class, which has the following attributes:
*   `seq_ix: int`: The ID for the current sequence.
*   `step_in_seq: int`: The step number within the sequence.
*   `need_prediction: bool`: Whether a prediction is required for this point.
*   `state: np.ndarray`: The current market state vector (containing p0..p11, v0..v11, dp0..1, dv0..1).

Your `predict` method should:
*   Return `None` when `need_prediction` is `False`.
*   Return a `numpy.ndarray` of shape `(2,)` when `need_prediction` is `True`.
*   Remember to manage and reset the model's state for each new sequence (`seq_ix`).

### Packaging your solution

Your solution might include more than just `solution.py` (e.g., model weight files, helper Python modules, configs). Make sure to include all necessary files in your zip archive.

You can create the zip archive from your solution directory with a command like this:

```bash
# From inside your solution folder (e.g., my_awesome_solution/)
# This command zips up everything in the current directory.
zip -r ../solution.zip .
```

> **Note:** Make sure `solution.py` is at the root level inside the zip archive, not inside another folder.

## What's in the box

We've provided the following files to help you:

*   `datasets/train.parquet`: A training dataset containing **10,721** sequences.
*   `datasets/valid.parquet`: A validation dataset containing **1,444** sequences. You can use this for local validation, but you are also free to create your own validation splits or strategies.
*   `utils.py`: Contains helper classes and the scoring function so you can check your performance locally.
*   `example_solution/solution.py`: A Vanilla GRU baseline solution generated by an LLM to show the required submission format.

Good luck, and have fun building! We can't wait to see what you create.

import os
import sys
import numpy as np

# Adjust path to import utils from parent directory
CURRENT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.append(f"{CURRENT_DIR}/..")

from utils import DataPoint, ScorerStepByStep
import onnxruntime as ort

class PredictionModel:
    """
    Baseline Solution (Vanilla GRU).
    
    This solution uses a simple GRU model trained on 32 features
    to predict t0 and t1.

    Note: This code was generated by an LLM as a baseline demonstration.
    """

    def __init__(self, model_path=""):
        self.current_seq_ix = None
        self.sequence_history = []
        
        # Determine paths
        base_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
        onnx_path = os.path.join(base_dir, "baseline.onnx")
        
        # Initialize ONNX Runtime Session
        sess_options = ort.SessionOptions()
        sess_options.intra_op_num_threads = 1
        sess_options.inter_op_num_threads = 1
        sess_options.graph_optimization_level = ort.GraphOptimizationLevel.ORT_ENABLE_ALL
        
        self.ort_session = None
        
        try:
            # Load ONNX Model
            self.ort_session = ort.InferenceSession(onnx_path, sess_options, providers=['CPUExecutionProvider'])
            self.input_name = self.ort_session.get_inputs()[0].name
            self.output_name = self.ort_session.get_outputs()[0].name
            print(f"Loaded ONNX model from {onnx_path}")
                
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error loading model resources: {e}")
            self.ort_session = None

    def predict(self, data_point: DataPoint) -> np.ndarray:
        # Reset state on new sequence
        if self.current_seq_ix != data_point.seq_ix:
            self.current_seq_ix = data_point.seq_ix
            self.sequence_history = []

        # Update history
        self.sequence_history.append(data_point.state.copy())

        # If prediction not needed yet, return None
        if not data_point.need_prediction:
            return None
            
        if self.ort_session is None:
            return np.zeros(2)

        # Prepare input window (last 100 steps)
        # The model was trained with a context window of 100
        history_window = self.sequence_history[-100:]
        
        # Pad with zeros if history is shorter than 100 (should not happen for need_prediction=True starting at step 99)
        if len(history_window) < 100:
             padding = [np.zeros_like(history_window[0])] * (100 - len(history_window))
             history_window = padding + history_window

        data_arr = np.asarray(history_window, dtype=np.float32)
        
        # Add batch dimension: (1, Sequence_Length, Features)
        data_tensor = np.expand_dims(data_arr, axis=0)
        
        # Run inference
        ort_inputs = {self.input_name: data_tensor}
        # Output shape from our VanillaLSTM is (1, 2) because we select the last step inside the model
        output = self.ort_session.run([self.output_name], ort_inputs)[0]
        
        if len(output.shape) == 3:
            # If model returns (Batch, Seq, Features)
            prediction = output[0, -1, :]
        else:
            # If model returns (Batch, Features)
            prediction = output[0]
            
        return prediction


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Local testing
    test_file = f"{CURRENT_DIR}/../datasets/valid.parquet"
    
    if os.path.exists(test_file):
        model = PredictionModel()
        scorer = ScorerStepByStep(test_file)
        
        print("Testing Vanilla GRU Baseline (ONNX)...")
        results = scorer.score(model)
        
        print("\nResults:")
        print(f"Mean Weighted Pearson correlation: {results['weighted_pearson']:.6f}")
        for i, target in enumerate(scorer.targets):
            print(f"  {target}: {results[target]:.6f}")
    else:
        print("Valid parquet not found for testing.")

1. `HIGH` Цель обучения не совпадает с целевой метрикой из-за клипа `y_true`.
Факты: клип таргета перед обоими loss ([train_vendor_residual_gru.py:253](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/train_vendor_residual_gru.py:253)), тогда как метрика клипает `y_pred`, а не `y_true` ([evaluation.py:19](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/evaluation.py:19)); веса loss тоже считаются по уже клипнутому `target` ([dl.py:116](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/dl.py:116), [dl.py:143](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/dl.py:143)).
Фикс: в Pearson-стадии использовать неклипнутый `y_true`; если нужен стабилизатор, клипать `pred` до `[-6, 6]` внутри loss.

2. `HIGH` Pearson оптимизируется по chunk-ам TBPTT, а валидируется глобально по всем scored-точкам.
Факты: loss считается отдельно в каждом chunk ([train_vendor_residual_gru.py:256](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/train_vendor_residual_gru.py:256)-[274](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/train_vendor_residual_gru.py:274)), при том что итоговая метрика считается глобально ([evaluation.py:41](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/evaluation.py:41)-[54](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/evaluation.py:54)).
Фикс: собирать предикты всех chunk-ов батча и считать один Pearson-loss на полном masked-наборе батча.

3. `MEDIUM` `sequence_reweighting` частично не работает и частично считает не то.

Фикс: считать seq-веса только по masked step-ам и использовать ту же логику в Pearson (или убрать флаг, если не нужен).

4. `MEDIUM` Нет finite-guard, из-за чего run может полностью развалиться на NaN.

{"status":{"completed":"1. `P0` Модель не тренируется в реальном inference-режиме (`tf=0`)  
Refs: [train_ar_gru.py:205](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/exp_ar_gru/train_ar_gru.py:205), [train_ar_gru.py:539](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/exp_ar_gru/train_ar_gru.py:539), [train_ar_gru.py:681](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/exp_ar_gru/train_ar_gru.py:681).  
Проблема: `teacher_forcing_end` по умолчанию `0.05`, то есть даже в конце free-stage остаются oracle-подмешивания. Для AR это критичный train/infer shift.  
Минимальный фикс:
```python
# parse_args
parser.add_argument("--teacher-forcing-end", type=float, default=0.0)
```
и/или принудительно:
```python
if use_pearson_loss:
    tf_prob = 0.0
```

2. `P1` Teacher forcing применяется и на warmup-шаги, где лосс не считается  
Refs: [train_ar_gru.py:310](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/exp_ar_gru/train_ar_gru.py:310), [train_ar_gru.py:315](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/exp_ar_gru/train_ar_gru.py:315), [ar_gru.py:124](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/ar_gru.py:124).  
Проблема: `mask_chunk` используется только в лоссе, но не ограничивает teacher forcing. В итоге модель в warmup часто видит oracle-state, а на inference warmup полностью autoregressive.  
Минимальный фикс: добавить `teacher_mask` в `forward_free_run_chunk` и разрешать teacher forcing только где `need_prediction_mask=True` (или хотя бы после `warmup_steps`).

3. `P1` Градиент AR-цепочки обрывается на каждом шаге  
Refs: [train_ar_gru.py:312](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/exp_ar_gru/train_ar_gru.py:312), [ar_gru.py:132](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/ar_gru.py:132).  
Проблема: `detach_prev_output=True` + `prev = next_prev.detach()` делает эффективный горизонт градиента по self-conditioning равным 1 шагу. Модель слабо учится стабилизировать собственный rollout.  
Минимальный фикс:
```python
# train_epoch_free(...)
detach_prev_output=False
```
(детач по chunk уже есть на [train_ar_gru.py:301](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/exp_ar_gru/train_ar_gru.py:301)).

4. `P2` `LockedDropout` в free-run фактически не “locked” по времени  
Refs: [ar_gru.py:117](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/ar_gru.py:117), [dl.py:20](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/dl.py:20).  
Проблема: dropout вызывается внутри step-loop по 1 timestep, маска каждый шаг новая; это не variational dropout и добавляет лишний шум в AR state dynamics.  
Минимальный фикс: применять одну маску на весь chunk (или временно выключить input variational dropout в free-stage).

5. `P3` Hardcode в inference chunking  
Refs: [train_ar_gru.py:377](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/exp_ar_gru/train_ar_gru.py:377).  
Проблема: `warmup_steps=1`, `chunk_size=200` захардкожены и не синхронизированы с конфигом. Это не главный корень провала, но ухудшает воспроизводимость/debug.  
Минимальный фикс: прокинуть `cfg.chunk_size` (и явно фиксировать выбранный `warmup_steps` через аргумент функции).

Если нужно, внесу эти минимальные правки сразу в код и дам diff."}}

1. `HIGH` Цель обучения не совпадает с целевой метрикой из-за клипа `y_true`.
Факты: клип таргета перед обоими loss ([train_vendor_residual_gru.py:253](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/train_vendor_residual_gru.py:253)), тогда как метрика клипает `y_pred`, а не `y_true` ([evaluation.py:19](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/evaluation.py:19)); веса loss тоже считаются по уже клипнутому `target` ([dl.py:116](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/dl.py:116), [dl.py:143](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/dl.py:143)).
Фикс: в Pearson-стадии использовать неклипнутый `y_true`; если нужен стабилизатор, клипать `pred` до `[-6, 6]` внутри loss.

2. `HIGH` Pearson оптимизируется по chunk-ам TBPTT, а валидируется глобально по всем scored-точкам.
Факты: loss считается отдельно в каждом chunk ([train_vendor_residual_gru.py:256](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/train_vendor_residual_gru.py:256)-[274](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/train_vendor_residual_gru.py:274)), при том что итоговая метрика считается глобально ([evaluation.py:41](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/evaluation.py:41)-[54](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/evaluation.py:54)).
Фикс: собирать предикты всех chunk-ов батча и считать один Pearson-loss на полном masked-наборе батча.

3. `MEDIUM` `sequence_reweighting` частично не работает и частично считает не то.
Факты: флаг есть в `LossConfig` ([dl.py:106](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/dl.py:106)), но применяется только в MSE ([dl.py:123](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/dl.py:123)-[127](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/dl.py:127)); в Pearson игнорируется ([dl.py:130](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/dl.py:130)-[157](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/dl.py:157)). Плюс seq-веса в MSE считаются по всем step-ам, включая warmup (`need_prediction=False`) ([dl.py:203](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/dl.py:203)-[210](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/src/models/dl.py:210)).
Фикс: считать seq-веса только по masked step-ам и использовать ту же логику в Pearson (или убрать флаг, если не нужен).

4. `MEDIUM` Нет finite-guard, из-за чего run может полностью развалиться на NaN.
Факты: `loss.backward()`/`optimizer.step()` без `isfinite`-проверок ([train_vendor_residual_gru.py:276](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/train_vendor_residual_gru.py:276)-[279](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/train_vendor_residual_gru.py:279)); в логе есть `loss=nan, rho=nan` с 1-й эпохи ([train.log:38](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/residual_runs/2026-02-27_01-23-51/train.log:38)); при отсутствии валидного best state скрипт падает ([train_vendor_residual_gru.py:489](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/train_vendor_residual_gru.py:489)).

5. `MEDIUM` Семантика vendor warmup теряется: `NaN` превращается в `0` без отдельного признака валидности.
Факты: vendor inference оставляет warmup как `NaN` ([infer_vendor_batched.py:93](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/infer_vendor_batched.py:93)-[108](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/infer_vendor_batched.py:108)); загрузчик заменяет на `0` ([train_vendor_residual_gru.py:197](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/train_vendor_residual_gru.py:197)); далее из этого строятся `vendor_prev`/`vendor_diff` ([train_vendor_residual_gru.py:204](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/train_vendor_residual_gru.py:204)-[210](/home/xeliaray/projects/LOB-One-Shot/experiments/vendor_features/train_vendor_residual_gru.py:210)).
Фикс: добавить `vendor_available` feature и разделить “missing warmup” от реального нуля (например, ffill + mask)."}}
